title: Mathematics
short: 14 NCERT chapters. Standard and Basic share the syllabus.
blurb: Fourteen chapters, seven units. **Algebra alone is 20 of the 80 marks** and Statistics + Probability adds 11 — half the paper sits in six chapters. Every chapter page carries the formula set, the standard method, the mistakes that cost marks and exam Q&A.
syllabus_note: Standard (041) and Basic (241) share this syllabus; Basic tests the same topics at a lower difficulty. Unit marks are from the official CBSE Class X curriculum.
books: - **Mathematics — Textbook for Class X**, NCERT (primary; every board question traces back here)
- Mathematics Exemplar Problems for Class X, NCERT (for the harder 4- and 5-mark questions)
- Laboratory Manual — Mathematics, secondary stage, NCERT (for the 5-mark lab activity in IA)
removed: - **Constructions** (old Chapter 11) — removed from the Class X book entirely.
- **Areas Related to Circles**: only sectors and segments of a circle remain; the rest of the old chapter was trimmed.

units.title: Unit I · Number Systems
units.desc: Euclid’s division lemma, HCF/LCM, irrationality proofs and terminating decimals.
tips: - Every one of these 6 marks is procedural. Do not lose them to careless long division.

units.title: Unit II · Algebra
units.desc: Polynomials, linear pairs, quadratics and AP — the single biggest unit in the paper.
tips: - Word problems on AP and on pairs of linear equations are the reliable 4-5 markers.

units.title: Unit III · Coordinate Geometry
units.desc: Distance formula, section formula, area of a triangle.
tips: - Shortest unit to finish. Bank these 6 marks early.

units.title: Unit IV · Geometry
units.desc: Similarity in triangles, Pythagoras, and tangents to a circle.
tips: - Learn the theorem statements word-perfect; the 1-mark “state the theorem” questions are free.

units.title: Unit V · Trigonometry
units.desc: Ratios, the standard table, identities, heights and distances.
tips: - Identities are proof-based: write the LHS-to-RHS chain, never both sides at once.

units.title: Unit VI · Mensuration
units.desc: Sectors and segments, and combinations of solids including the frustum.
tips: - Units. Almost every loss of a mark here is a missing or wrong unit at the end.

units.title: Unit VII · Statistics & Probability
units.desc: Mean, median and mode of grouped data, ogives, and classical probability.
tips: - The most scoring unit per hour of study. Do it before you polish Geometry.

assessment: Theory paper — Section A (objective), B, C, D and case-based Section E
Accuracy and steps. Show the formula before substituting.
Internal assessment — pen-paper test + multiple assessment, portfolio, lab activity
Keep the lab manual and portfolio current through the year.
Total
Three hours for the theory paper.
study_order: **Algebra first** (20 marks, Chapters 2–5) — the biggest single block of marks.
**Statistics and Probability** (11 marks) — short chapters, high yield.
**Trigonometry** (12 marks) — the ratio table unlocks both chapters.
**Geometry** (15 marks) — theorem statements first, then the proof practice.
**Mensuration** (10) and **Coordinate Geometry** (6) — formula-driven.
**Number Systems** (6) last — the quickest unit to revise the night before.
Then two timed full papers with the official marking scheme.
countdown: Target: February–March 2027 boards. Confirm the official date sheet when CBSE publishes it.
practical_note: The 20 internal marks include a pen-paper test, multiple assessment, a portfolio and a **lab activity from the NCERT Laboratory Manual**.
practical: - **Lab activity (5 marks)**: usually a hands-on verification — for example verifying the basic proportionality theorem with a cut-out triangle, or the relationship between the surface area of a sphere and a circumscribing cylinder.
- **Portfolio (5 marks)**: your assignment sheets, the two chapter tests and one model/working file.
- **What to keep ready**: a clean geometry box, squared paper for graphs and ogives, and every assignment submitted on time — multiple assessment is largely built from those.
- Graphs: use a sharp pencil, label both axes, mark the scale, and give the graph a title. Unlabelled axes lose a step mark.

title: Science
short: 13 NCERT chapters across Chemistry, Biology and Physics.
blurb: Thirteen chapters, five units. **Chemistry and Biology are 25 marks each** — half the paper is Chapters 1 to 8. Each chapter page has the concept, the diagram or numerical method, the memory trick and exam Q&A.
syllabus_note: The rationalised NCERT Class X Science book has 13 chapters. Chapter 8 is now titled **Heredity** (older books say “Heredity and Evolution”).
books: - **Science — Textbook for Class X**, NCERT (the board paper is set from this book, including the activities)
- NCERT Exemplar Problems for Class X Science (for case-based and higher-order questions)
- CBSE Laboratory Manual for Class X (the practical exam is drawn from these activities)
removed: - Chapter 8 no longer covers the full evolution section; it is now **Heredity**.

units.title: Unit I · Chemical Substances
units.desc: Reactions and equations, acids bases salts, metals and non-metals, carbon compounds.
tips: - Balancing equations and the reaction types are asked every single year.

units.title: Unit II · World of Living
units.desc: Life processes, control and coordination, reproduction, heredity.
tips: - Diagrams carry marks. Draw them large, label with a ruler, and never shade.

units.title: Unit III · Natural Phenomena
units.desc: Light — reflection and refraction, the human eye and the colourful world.
tips: - Ray diagrams follow rules; learn the six standard cases and every numerical becomes mechanical.

units.title: Unit IV · Effects of Current
units.desc: Electricity and magnetic effects of current.
tips: - Series vs parallel numericals are the most repeated Physics questions.

units.title: Unit V · Natural Resources
units.desc: Our Environment — food chains, trophic levels, ozone and waste.
tips: - Small chapter, guaranteed marks. The 10% energy-transfer numerical appears often.

assessment: Theory paper — objective, short answer, long answer and case-based/source-based
Diagrams labelled; equations balanced; units written.
Practical / internal assessment — lab exam, practical file, two periodic tests, subject enrichment
The practical file must match the activity list exactly.
Total
Three hours for the theory paper.
study_order: **Chemistry (Chapters 1–4)** first — 25 marks and largely self-contained.
**Biology (Chapters 5–8)** next — another 25 marks, diagram-heavy.
**Electricity and Magnetism (11–12)** — 13 marks of mostly numericals.
**Optics (9–10)** — 12 marks; do ray diagrams before the numericals.
**Our Environment (13)** — quick 5 marks.
Then one timed paper, with the marking scheme open while you check it.
countdown: The practical exam is usually held in January–February, before the theory paper. Confirm with your school.
practical_note: The 20 internal marks include a **practical examination** on the NCERT activities plus a practical file.
practical: - **Typical practical list**: properties of acids/bases with indicators; the reaction of metals with acid and with salt solutions; the reactivity series; properties of acetic acid; binary fission in amoeba and budding in yeast; CO₂ release in respiration; dependence of current on potential difference; series and parallel resistance; properties of a convex lens; and the parts of a dicot seed embryo.
- **Practical file format per activity**: aim, apparatus/materials, theory (one or two lines), procedure, observation table with units, result, precautions.
- **Diagram rules**: pencil only, no shading, labels on one side with horizontal guide lines, magnification not required.
- **Viva**: expect “why this precaution?” and “what does this observation prove?” — the reason matters more than the reading.

title: Social Science
short: One paper, four disciplines, 20 marks each.
blurb: History, Geography, Political Science and Economics in **one three-hour paper, 20 marks each**. Plus map pointing, which is the cheapest marks in the whole board. Each chapter page gives the answer frame CBSE actually rewards.
syllabus_note: Four separate NCERT books. Several chapters still printed in older copies are **not** assessed — see below.
removed: - **Popular Struggles and Movements** — full chapter removed.
- **The Age of Industrialisation** is still printed in the History book but is **not** assessed in the board paper.
- **The Making of a Global World**: only subtopics 1 to 1.3 are examined.
- **Manufacturing Industries**: much of the old industry-by-industry detail was trimmed.
- **Lifelines of National Economy**: map pointing only.

units.title: History
units.desc: India and the Contemporary World II — nationalism, the global world and print culture.
tips: - Write dates and names. Answers without dates score badly in History.

units.title: Geography
units.desc: Contemporary India II — resources, water, agriculture, minerals, industry.
tips: - Always give an Indian example with a name and a state.

units.title: Political Science
units.desc: Democratic Politics II — power sharing, federalism, parties, outcomes.
tips: - Five short chapters, the highest marks-per-hour in the subject.

units.title: Economics
units.desc: Understanding Economic Development — development, sectors, credit, globalisation.
tips: - Definitions plus one example each. That is the whole answer format.

assessment: Theory — History 20, Geography 20, Political Science 20, Economics 20
Points, not paragraphs. Five distinct points for a 5-mark answer.
Map work — printed inside the History and Geography sections
included
Pure recall from the official list of map items. Do not skip it.
Internal assessment — periodic tests, the Economics project, portfolio
The Consumer Rights project is the usual internal project.
Total
Three hours for the whole paper.
study_order: **Political Science first** — five short chapters, 20 marks, fastest to finish.
**Economics** — five chapters, definition-plus-example answers.
**Geography**, and do the map items as you go rather than leaving them to the end.
**History** last — the longest reading, so start it early in the year and revise late.
Then one full three-hour paper: the real difficulty here is finishing in time, not the content.
countdown: Download the current session’s **list of map items** from CBSE Academic — it changes between sessions.
practical_note: Social Science has no lab exam, but it has **map work inside the paper** and a project in the internal assessment.
practical: - **Map items (History)**: centres of the 1857 revolt, Congress sessions, sites of the Non-Cooperation and Civil Disobedience movements, major plantations and industrial regions.
- **Map items (Geography)**: dams, soil types, major crops, mineral belts, oil fields, steel plants, cotton and woollen textile centres, software parks, sea ports and airports.
- **How to practise**: take a blank political outline map of India and point every item from the official list without looking. Repeat until you can do the whole list in ten minutes.
- **Project**: the Consumer Rights chapter is assessed as project work — a survey of a local shop, an ISI/BIS label study, or a consumer-court case write-up all work well.

title: English Language & Literature
short: First Flight, Footprints Without Feet, grammar and writing.
blurb: Nine prose chapters, ten poems and nine supplementary chapters — but **roughly a third of the paper is Reading and Writing**, not literature at all. Each page carries the summary, the themes, the extract answers and the word meanings.
syllabus_note: First Flight (main reader), Footprints Without Feet (supplementary reader) and Words and Expressions II (workbook).
books: - **Words and Expressions II** — workbook for grammar and writing
removed: - **The Hundred Dresses I** and **The Hundred Dresses II** — both prose chapters removed.
- **The Hack Driver** — removed from Footprints Without Feet.
- Older question banks still print all of these. Ignore them.

units.title: First Flight · Prose
units.desc: The main reader. Reference-to-context extracts and long answers come mostly from here.
tips: - Know the narrator of every chapter — that is the most common extract question.

units.title: First Flight · Poems
units.desc: Ten short poems. Theme, central idea and poetic devices.
tips: - Learn the central idea of each in one sentence; the extract question is worth 3–4 marks.

units.title: Footprints Without Feet
units.desc: The supplementary reader. Read fast; answers are short.
tips: - Shortest chapters first: The Thief’s Story, The Midnight Visitor, A Question of Trust.

units.title: Reading, Grammar & Writing
units.desc: Unseen passages, note-making, grammar in context, letter, article and analytical paragraph.
tips: - These marks are earned by format. Practise the exact word limits.

assessment: Section A — Reading skills: unseen passage plus note-making and summarising
Format marks are awarded separately. Follow the note-making format exactly.
Section B — Writing and grammar: letter, article or analytical paragraph, grammar in context
Stick to the word limit; exceed it and you run out of time.
Section C — Literature: First Flight and Footprints Without Feet
Answers in your own words. Copying lines from the book scores badly.
Total theory
Three hours.
Internal assessment — listening and speaking, plus a reading/reading-aloud project
The ASL speaking test is scheduled by your school.
study_order: **Writing formats first** — letter, article, analytical paragraph. 20 marks that depend only on format.
**Poems** — ten short texts, quick to finish, reliably asked.
**Footprints Without Feet** — nine short chapters.
**First Flight prose** — the longest reading; do the two-part chapters early.
**Grammar in context** — tense, modals, subject-verb agreement, reported speech, determiners.
Then one unseen passage a day for a fortnight; this is a speed skill, not a knowledge skill.
countdown: The listening and speaking assessment is usually held in December–January.
practical_note: English internal assessment is **listening and speaking**, not a lab exam.
practical: - **Speaking (10 marks)**: usually a short picture description or topic-based speech, followed by a brief interaction. Marks go to fluency, accuracy and pronunciation — not to how fancy your vocabulary is.
- **Listening (10 marks)**: a recorded passage with comprehension questions. Practise note-taking while listening; you cannot rewind.
- **Reading project**: an assessment of reading and reading aloud, set by your school.
- **Preparation that works**: record yourself speaking for two minutes on a random topic, then listen back. Two weeks of this moves the speaking score more than any textbook.

title: Hindi
short: Course A: क्षितिज + कृतिका. Course B: स्पर्श + संचयन.
blurb: Two courses, same 80 + 20 split. **Course A** covers क्षितिज भाग-2 and कृतिका भाग-2; **Course B** covers स्पर्श भाग-2 and संचयन भाग-2. Grammar and writing together are worth more than the literature section — do not study them last.
syllabus_note: Study only the course your school offers. Both are here so you can ignore one.
removed: - From क्षितिज भाग-2: **सवैया और कवित्त** (देव), **छाया मत छूना** (गिरिजा कुमार माथुर), **कन्यादान** (ऋतुराज), **मानवीय करुणा की दिव्य चमक** (जैनेन्द्र कुमार) and **स्त्री शिक्षा के विरोधी कुतर्कों का खंडन** (शेखर जोशी).
- From स्पर्श भाग-2: **दोहे**, **मधुर-मधुर मेरे दीपक जल** and **गिरगिट**.

units.title: Course A · क्षितिज भाग-2
units.desc: The main reader — prose and poetry carrying the largest share of the literature marks.
tips: - पद्य पाठों के लिए कवि-परिचय और काव्य-सौंदर्य याद रखें।

units.title: Course A · कृतिका भाग-2
units.desc: Three long prose chapters, asked as 50–60 word answers.
tips: - केवल तीन पाठ — पूरे अंक आसानी से मिल सकते हैं।

units.title: Course B · स्पर्श भाग-2
units.desc: काव्य खंड और गद्य खंड — the Course B main reader.
tips: - काव्य खंड पहले पढ़ें — पद्य छोटे होते हैं।

units.title: Course B · संचयन भाग-2
units.desc: Three supplementary stories.
tips: - तीनों कहानियों के मुख्य पात्र और कथानक याद रखें।

units.title: व्याकरण और लेखन
units.desc: Grammar in context, plus पत्र, अनुच्छेद, संदेश and विज्ञापन लेखन.
tips: - शब्द-सीमा का पालन करें — यही अंक काटने का सबसे बड़ा कारण है।

assessment: अपठित गद्यांश — unseen comprehension
गति और शब्द-चयन। हर दूसरे दिन एक गद्यांश।
व्याकरण — grammar in context
रटने से नहीं, अभ्यास से।
पाठ्यपुस्तक और पूरक पाठ्यपुस्तक
उत्तर अपने शब्दों में, पाठ की पंक्तियाँ न लिखें।
रचनात्मक लेखन — letter, article, message, advertisement
प्रारूप के अंक अलग मिलते हैं।
Total theory
तीन घंटे।
Internal assessment — listening, speaking and reading project
ASL विद्यालय द्वारा निर्धारित।
study_order: **व्याकरण और लेखन पहले** — लगभग 36 अंक, केवल अभ्यास पर निर्भर।
**कृतिका / संचयन** — तीन-तीन पाठ, तेज़ी से पूरे होते हैं।
**क्षितिज / स्पर्श का काव्य खंड** — पद्य छोटे, अंक अधिक।
**गद्य खंड** — सबसे लंबा पठन, वर्ष की शुरुआत में शुरू करें।
फिर हर दूसरे दिन एक अपठित गद्यांश — यह गति का अभ्यास है, ज्ञान का नहीं।
countdown: श्रवण और वाचन मूल्यांकन आमतौर पर दिसंबर–जनवरी में होता है।
practical_note: हिंदी का आंतरिक मूल्यांकन **श्रवण एवं वाचन (ASL)** है।
practical: - **वाचन (10 अंक)**: चित्र वर्णन या विषय पर संक्षिप्त भाषण, फिर कुछ प्रश्न। प्रवाह, शुद्धता और उच्चारण पर अंक मिलते हैं।
- **श्रवण (10 अंक)**: रिकॉर्ड किया गया गद्यांश और उस पर प्रश्न। सुनते समय संक्षिप्त टिप्पणी लिखने का अभ्यास करें।
- **अभ्यास**: मोबाइल पर किसी भी विषय पर दो मिनट बोलकर रिकॉर्ड करें और सुनें। दो सप्ताह में सबसे अधिक सुधार इसी से होता है।

title: Information Technology
short: 20 chapters, practical-first. Already published as its own hub.
